looks_like: SQL built with an f-string from caller-supplied column names
why_fine: The names are keyword arguments from internal service code and are checked against the _SUBSCRIPTION_COLUMNS allow-list before use, and values stay bound parameters.

looks_like: SQL injection through an f-string IN clause
why_fine: The interpolated text is only a run of ? placeholders, and the ids are bound parameters that the route has already converted to integers.

looks_like: Tenant leak: query with no tenant filter
why_fine: It is a system-level query for the worker, which must see every tenant, and each row carries its own tenant_id, which is used for all later access.

looks_like: Tenant leak: invoice lookup with no tenant filter
why_fine: Webhooks carry no tenant context and gateway charge ids are globally unique, so the charge id identifies the invoice on its own.

looks_like: Unsalted fast hash used for credentials
why_fine: API keys are long machine-generated tokens rather than passwords, so brute force and rainbow tables do not apply, and a deterministic hash is what allows lookup by key.
This is retry backoff jitter, with no security role.
It only computes an HTTP ETag, is marked usedforsecurity=False, and needs no collision resistance.
It applies only to the public plan catalog, which the README says is public, has no credentials and is read-only.
The README lists it as public, and it returns only a status and version string.
The README lists the catalog as public, and it holds only published prices.
Both sides are ISO 8601 calendar dates, whose lexical order matches chronological order, and the comparison correctly lets a coupon work on its expiry day.
period_days is the only divisor and comes from days_inclusive, which is at least 1 for any valid period.

looks_like: Broad except Exception in a loop
why_fine: It rolls back, logs with a full traceback and continues so one subscription cannot block the rest, and the sweep retries it next time.

looks_like: Unimplemented methods with ... as the body
why_fine: This is a typing.Protocol, whose method bodies are meant to be empty, and the real implementations are GatewayClient and the test fake.
